public_rationale: On the ordinary tool-level reading, merely is too strong. Before publication, Amazon Q Developer included code-security scanning, so a generative coding assistant could do more than produce plausible text. The narrower statement that language models use token prediction is supported as technical context. That training objective does not establish the limits of a complete product.
limitations: This result depends on reading AI tool as the complete coding assistant, rather than only its base model.
The example concerns Amazon Q Developer and does not establish every Copilot capability.
Security scanning neither guarantees secure output nor establishes human-like understanding.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: An AI coding tool merely guesses what code looks right, given the prompt it was provided.

our_interpretation: The context limits AI tool to generative coding assistants.
The ordinary tool-level reading is that these assistants only generate plausible code and do not also analyze or check code.
I assess the first half of 2024 as the latest complete pre-publication product observation window.
A model’s prediction objective and a complete coding tool’s capabilities are different questions.
This does not treat the claim as a statement about consciousness or require tools to guarantee secure code.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous implementations establish that the relevant coding tools only generate plausible continuations, without substantive code analysis or verification.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A contemporaneous generative coding assistant demonstrably includes substantive code analysis or verification beyond generating plausible text.
